assets.prompt: Redesign the referenced event poster completely as a credible contemporary Mexican neighborhood cultural event flyer prepared by a careful local graphic designer. Flat print-ready portrait 1024x1536, no photograph of a poster, no mockup. Restrained two-color screenprint, charcoal black and deep burnt orange on clean warm ivory uncoated stock, very subtle real ink texture, generous margins, confident typographic grid. Typography dominates 65% of the design: condensed bold clean block lettering, editorial hierarchy, aligned small sans-serif labels; no fake distressed lettering, no ornate Victorian borders, no excessive faux vintage noise. One simple bold cut-paper style skeletal face in a black witch hat, deliberately spare asymmetric hand-inked shapes with a few coarse hatch marks, and three small marigolds; striking macabre silhouette, no detailed AI fantasy Catrina, no cinematic lighting, no 3D, no elaborate cityscape, no ghost crowd. Make it feel like an actual community poster from a print shop, readable on WhatsApp. Exact Spanish text, carefully spelled, all readable: small top 'COMITÉ 2026 INVITA'; enormous title on three lines 'CALLE DE' / 'LAS BRUJAS' / '2026'; strong orange badge '24 AÑOS DE TRADICIÓN'; medium 'DÍA DE MUERTOS'; clear large date '2 DE NOVIEMBRE'; time 'CITA · 5:30 P. M.'; location 'CALLE ALLENDE'; small bottom 'DESFILE · DISFRACES · SHOWS'; final footer 'Ven con tu carro, moto o disfraz'. Do not add any other text or logos. Use reference only for event identity; this must be a visibly new graphic design, substantially less busy.
